content.text:
I submitted index 24 (La 0.41, Sb 0.59), but that choice means little: none of the compositions I measured showed any real photoresponse.

**EQE results (all 3 merit measurements used):**

| Index | La / Sb | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|
| 12 | 0.74 / 0.26 | -0.0063 |
| 24 | 0.41 / 0.59 | -0.0015 |
| 28 | 0.32 / 0.68 | -0.0045 |

All three values are essentially zero and within noise. Index 24 is the highest only nominally.

**Why I think the whole line is inactive:** La–Sb oxides are wide-gap materials (roughly 3 eV or more), so they shouldn't absorb the 2.1 eV light used here. The flat, zero result fits that.

**XRD (3 of 5 scans used, on indexes 4, 12 and 21):** each pattern was dominated by what look like substrate peaks, with only weak, poorly defined film peaks. None pointed to a lower-gap phase worth chasing. I didn't compare the patterns against simulated ones with `match_xrd`, so the phases aren't identified.

**What this leaves uncovered:** I didn't measure the La-rich end (indexes 0–11) or the gaps between my points. With only three measurements and all readings at noise level, I can't rule out a small active spot I missed. Still, nothing in the data or the chemistry suggests one exists.
